claims.statement: hypermnesic reaches external agent hosts through three deliberately separate integration surfaces — an in-repo Claude Code/Codex marketplace pack that speaks MCP over HTTP, an in-repo Hermes Agent pack that speaks only to the local `hypermnesic` CLI, and an out-of-repo Obsidian companion — and the Hermes pack consumes neither the Claude/Codex manifests nor their MCP wiring.

The repository intentionally carries two Claude marketplace listings: the repo-root `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` makes a no-checkout GitHub install possible (Claude Code only discovers `marketplace.json` at a checkout root, never in a subdirectory), while `plugin/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` serves the local `plugin/`-directory source; the root listing's plugin entry points at `./plugin/plugins/hypermnesic` and declares no `version` or `description`, so those live solely in the plugin manifest and the two listings cannot drift.

The Claude plugin manifest declares only a skills path and must not reference the standard `hooks/hooks.json`, because Claude Code auto-loads that file and a manifest `hooks` key pointing at the same path is a duplicate that fails the entire plugin load — taking both the skill and the hooks down; the constraint is pinned by a regression test.

The Codex plugin manifest declares the same shared skills directory plus an `interface` block that points at the same `hooks/hooks.json` and declares `--host codex` as its host flag; the hook script accepts `--host claude|codex`, and that host value both selects the per-host disable switch and is written into the status record.

The bundled `.mcp.json` is OAuth-discovery-only — a `streamable-http` server whose URL is templated from `HYPERMNESIC_MCP_URL`, with no `auth` block, no `token_env`, and no static `Authorization` header — because a static header would suppress the OAuth discovery the host performs from `{type, url}` alone; the first connect is one browser authorization (read by default, `write` approved at the consent page to enable `commit_note`).

The published plugin tree is distribution-generic and secret-free: tests scan every file under `plugin/` for committed credential material and for operator-specific values (tailnet hostname, specific CGNAT IPs, absolute home paths), and assert the MCP wiring keeps its env-templated URL.

`plugin/plugins/hypermnesic/hooks/hooks.json` wires exactly one `UserPromptSubmit` event to `hypermnesic_agent_hook.py --host claude` with a 6-second timeout, with no `SessionStart` preamble and no Bash interception.

The auto-recall hook is non-blocking by contract: every path through `handle()` returns a continue response and context is added only through `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`; a malformed payload prints a diagnostic to stderr and still emits a clean continue with exit code 0; and any event that is not a prompt-submit variant is inert and writes no status record.

Before any network call the hook evaluates gates in a fixed order — disabled state, prompt relevance, endpoint configured, credential available, non-empty query — and each rung maps to its own stable outcome code (`disabled_global`/`disabled_host`, `off_topic`, `unconfigured_endpoint`, `missing_credential`), so an off-topic or unconfigured prompt performs no lookup.

The Claude/Codex hook's relevance gate accepts memory-ish phrasing from a fixed term list OR a multi-word capitalized proper noun, while the Hermes pack's equivalent gate is weaker — a minimum message length plus a term list, with no proper-noun branch.

The hook's lookup is one bounded JSON-RPC `tools/call` for `search` with `k=5` under a 2.5-second cap, and at most five hits are injected as `path: heading — snippet` with snippets flattened to one line and trimmed to 200 characters; newline flattening also applies to `path` and `heading` so a stored note cannot forge extra lines in the injected context.

The auto-recall hook has a credential path separate from MCP OAuth because Claude Code exposes no stored MCP OAuth token to hook subprocesses: its working remote path is the auth-off tailnet read route that needs only a URL, so `HYPERMNESIC_MCP_TOKEN` is optional, is used only in the `Authorization` header, is never echoed to stdout/stderr/injected text, and a non-tailnet endpoint without a token stops at `missing_credential` instead of sending an unauthenticated request.

The hook recognizes the token-free tailnet read route structurally: a URL whose host parses as an IP in the `100.` CGNAT range is classified `tailnet_read` (and needs no credential), while `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` is `local`, an `https://` origin is `public_https`, and anything else is `other`.

Every prompt-submit run records a non-secret status record out of band with a stable `last_outcome`, a plain-language explanation, the host, enabled/disabled state, endpoint and credential categories, hit count, degraded flag and timestamps — never the prompt, endpoint URL, token, `Authorization` header, or raw large snippets — so an owner can diagnose why recall did or did not inject without reading hook source.

The hook status record defaults to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/hypermnesic/hook-status.json` and can be redirected with `HYPERMNESIC_HOOK_STATUS_FILE`; writes merge the new record over the previous one (preserving the last successful `last_recall_at`), are written via a temp file and rename, are wrapped so an unwritable path can never block the hook, and a missing file reads back as `never_run` rather than an error.

The plugin ships a status helper script (not a `hypermnesic` CLI subcommand) whose `test-recall` mode runs the same bounded lookup path for an explicit query, prints sanitized path/heading/snippet previews capped at 240/160/200 characters, and flags the record `test_initiated` so a diagnostic run is distinguishable from real traffic.

`HYPERMNESIC_HOOK_DISABLE_LOOKUP=1` disables proactive recall for the whole plugin install and `HYPERMNESIC_HOOK_DISABLED_HOSTS` disables it for the named hosts; both are evaluated before the relevance gate so a disabled hook does no work, and disabling auto-recall leaves the MCP tools available through OAuth discovery and the local CLI untouched.

The Hermes pack is CLI-first: `plugin/hermes/plugin.yaml` declares the `pre_llm_call` hook it provides and requires only the non-secret `HYPERMNESIC_REPO`, and `register(ctx)` always registers the namespaced `hypermnesic-memory` skill while registering the recall hook only when `HYPERMNESIC_HERMES_RECALL` is truthy.

When enabled, the Hermes recall hook runs `hypermnesic retrieve <repo> <query> --k 3 --now --json` (plus `--index-db` when `HYPERMNESIC_INDEX_DB` is set) under a 3-second timeout and returns at most three hits within a 1400-character context cap, with query/path/heading/snippet bounds of 500/180/120/280 characters; an irrelevant message, unset repo, missing CLI, subprocess error, non-zero exit, unparseable JSON, empty hit list, or timeout all return `None`, which is silence.

Hermes plugin skills load in the namespaced view (`hypermnesic:hypermnesic-memory`) and are absent from the flat available-skills index, so the pack ships an optional flat export at `plugin/hermes/flat-skill/hypermnesic-memory/` that an operator can copy into an ordinary skills directory, and a test requires that flat copy to stay byte-identical to the namespaced skill.

Tests enforce that the Hermes package carries no MCP transport or credential assumptions and no Claude/Codex loader assumptions — no `.mcp.json`, MCP CLI commands, `HYPERMNESIC_MCP_TOKEN`, `Authorization`/`Bearer`, `UserPromptSubmit`, or `.claude-plugin`/`.codex-plugin` references — and no operator-specific values or secrets, which is what keeps the two packs independent rather than accidentally coupled.

The Obsidian companion ships from a separate public repository under GPL-3.0-or-later (first release 0.3.0) while the engine here is AGPL-3.0-only, and neither is a derivative of the other because they are separate processes communicating only at arm's length over the read-only MCP wire (`search`/`build_context`/`think`) with no shared or statically linked code — a boundary that holds only while the companion does not vendor, import, or statically link engine source.

The Obsidian companion is strictly read-only and enforces that with a static read-only invariant scan in its own suite (`test/read-only.test.ts`, ported from the former `tests/test_obsidian_plugin.py` in this repository, which no longer exists); write, cleanup, revoke, forget/delete, and revert stay in the git-first CLI/MCP surfaces, so a read-only client cannot bypass consent, write scope, protected-path refusals, or server-side write guards.

Every distributed version string must agree with the `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` authority and the `src/hypermnesic/__init__.py` mirror; `scripts/check_version_consistency.py` names each slot it checks (including nested marketplace `plugins[].version` entries) and fails the build on drift instead of the slots being hand-enumerated or synchronized.

Because the plugin trees are configuration and prose consumed by host harnesses rather than by the engine runtime, their correctness properties are validated statically in the offline suite — marketplace source resolution, manifest required fields, no duplicate hooks declaration, skill frontmatter and real tool names, user-neutral content, secret-freedom, discovery-only MCP wiring, hook behavior and outcome recording, and the Hermes contracts — with a live install on both hosts as the separate manual verification.
